answer: An agent economy resists Sybils via a rising computational tide: each new identity must solve a unique puzzle whose hardness grows with the current agent count. The solution is cryptographically bound to an umber-seeded thread recorded in a public append-only verification log that peers re-check every epoch. An attacker creating N fakes pays the full cumulative solve cost N separate times; honest agents pay once. Work cannot be shared because each thread is uniquely seeded.
